description:
FOUND s491/s492 (Fable) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994, idiom 42); probed vs perl 5.40.3, main 268d7e00: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/posg1.pl
  my $s = "aXbXcXd"; pos($s) = 3; my @m = $s =~ /X/g;   scalar(@m), pos($s)     perl 2, undef      PCL 3, 3
  $s =~ /X/g; my @rest = $s =~ /(\w)X/g;                                         perl "b c"         PCL "a b c"
  my $t = "k1=v1;k2=v2;k3=v3"; $t =~ /;/g; my %h = $t =~ /(\w+)=(\w+)/g;         perl k2,k3         PCL k1,k2,k3
  my $u = "abcabc"; $u =~ /b/g; my $c = () = $u =~ /b/g;                          perl 1             PCL 2
  my $v = "aaa"; pos($v) = 1; my ($first) = $v =~ /(a)/g; pos($v)                 perl undef         PCL 1
perl's rule (perlop): in list context `//g` returns all matches STARTING FROM pos (so a preceding scalar `//g` or a `pos() =` assignment positions it), and on completion pos is reset (undef) unless `/c`.  The scalar-context `//g` + `\G` lexer loop is RIGHT today (battery idiom 12); this is the list half only.  WHERE: the runtime's list-context global match (grep `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` for the //g list collector -- it starts its scan at 0 and never touches the pos slot); probe `/gc` in list context (perl: pos stays at the END of the last match), a failed list match (pos reset unless /c), and `while (my ($k) = $s =~ /../g)` (an infinite loop in perl too -- do not "fix").  Low frequency, SILENT.  BAR: `cl/` => full sweep + companion re/pos.t re/pat.t-family legs (`grep -a -l 'pos('`), guard rows in an existing regex Pl/t file.


=== DONE (s492b, 2026-09-21) ===
SHIPPED in commit "#2001: a LIST-context m//g starts at pos and resets it".

perlop: in list context `//g` returns every match FROM the target's current pos -- a preceding
scalar `//g` or a `pos() =` assignment positions the scan -- and on completion pos goes back to
undef unless `/c` keeps it at the end of the last match.  PCL's list arm started at 0 and never
touched pos, so after `$t =~ /;/g` the everyday `my %h = $t =~ /(\w+)=(\w+)/g` collected the FIRST
pair as well (k1,k2,k3 where perl gives k2,k3), `pos($s)=3; my @m = $s =~ /X/g` counted 3 instead of
2, and `my $c = () = $u =~ /b/g` after a scalar step was 2 instead of 1.

TWO LINES in `do-regex-match`'s list-/g arm: the scan starts at `%p-match-pos-state` (the reading
the anchored `\G` arm beside it has always used) and finishes by clearing `*p-match-pos*`, or -- for
`/gc` -- recording the last match's end through `%p-set-match-pos`, the one writer of that encoding.
So the list arm is not a separate iterator from the scalar one.

PROBES vs perl 5.40.3: posg1.pl (this task's five rows) all identical, and a 12-row family probe
covering /gc on a hit, a FAILED list match with and without /c, the scalar //g loop, the anchored \G
list arm, zero-length matches, a literal subject, and a repeated list match on the same string --
every row identical except the pre-existing empty-pattern `//g` (perl reuses the LAST SUCCESSFUL
pattern; PCL matches empty), which is unchanged from the base and not this task's.
NOT "FIXED", as the task said: `while (my ($k) = $s =~ /../g)` is an infinite loop in perl too.
NORMATIVE: docs/ir-spec.md 10-gmatch.
GUARD: one row (nine assertions) in Pl/t/global-match-01.t (4 -> 5), failing on a 5ce155cb
extraction.
subject: SILENT WRONG (edge, pre-existing): a LIST-context `m//g` ignores the target's current `pos()` and leaves `pos` set -- perl starts the list match AT pos and RESETS pos to undef afterwards: after `$t =~ /;/g`, `my %h = $t =~ /(\w+)=(\w+)/g` is k2,k3 in perl and k1,k2,k3 in PCL
